page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. This instance features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing and text processing, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks are relatively weak. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU score fall into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds measuring 32.39 GB/sec and 20.69 GB/sec respectively, and Passmark database operations scoring in the bottom 25 percent.

Given the high memory allocation relative to the vCPU count, this server offers a qualitative resource density advantage for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for single-threaded tasks, text processing, basic web serving, and lightweight LLM inference, where it processes 135M model prompts at 443.85 tokens per second. However, the weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth make it less optimal for heavy database operations or highly parallelized computational tasks.
